messages:
alex_nguyen: heads up — since the kernel-selection rollout yesterday we've seen a ~22% drop in prefix cache hit-rate for EU-west regions. noticed started around 03:12 UTC.
maya_li: wow that's sizable. is this KV keying mismatch or just cold starts from routing changes?
alex_nguyen: initial profiling suggests two things: (1) kernel changes slightly altered tokenization edge-cases for prompt normalization, which affects cache keys; (2) routing policy now sends a bigger fraction of traffic to cold replicas in eu-west during scale events.
tom_baker: logs? any examples of non-matching cache keys we can grep for?
alex_nguyen: pasted a short sample from the cache debugger:

```
[2026-03-15T03:12:21Z] request_id=rpc-42 prompt_hash=0x7f2a3a key=prefix_v2::model-ggml::len-32::norm-"What is\n" -> MISS
[2026-03-15T03:12:21Z] request_id=rpc-43 prompt_hash=0x7f2a3a key=prefix_v1::model-ggml::len-32::norm-"What is"   -> HIT
```

alex_nguyen: note the norm string has an extra newline after the kernel change; that leads to different keys.
maya_li: ah that newline normalization change slipped through token-normalizer when swapping tokenization kernel. regression then.
priya_shah: can we patch normalizer to canonicalize whitespace? also what's the impact on warmup strategies?
tom_baker: patching normalizer is quick, but rollout needs care. in parallel, we should reduce routing of new sessions to cold eu-west nodes — redirect to warm regional pool until cache warms.
maya_li: propose: (A) immediate hotfix to normalize whitespace in cache key creation, (B) temporary routing tweak: prefer warm host affinity for 20m, (C) run targeted primer job to pre-populate KV for top-5 prefix shards in eu-west.
alex_nguyen: Agreed. did some sim of primer job — a 10k request primer to each shard brought hit-rate from 38% -> 72% in ~7 minutes on staging.
priya_shah: what's the primer job cost? and will it overload burst capacity?
alex_nguyen: cost ~0.8 ETHU per 10k primer (cheap compared to user cost). We can throttle primer at 50rps per pod to avoid saturating.

infra-bot: deploybot: kernel-selection v2.1 rolled to prod @ 2026-03-14T22:40Z
infra-bot: rate-limiter: temporarily increasing burst tokens for primer tasks in eu-west until 04:20 UTC

maya_li: Tom, can you add a routing override rule that pins new sessions to warm hosts for 30m or until hit-rate > 60%? Something feature-flagged.
tom_baker: i'll add a feature-flagged policy under smart-routing: prefer_warm_affinity with cooldown. patch draft:

```
policy {
  name: prefer_warm_affinity
  target_region: eu-west
  warm_threshold: 0.6
  cooldown: 1800  # seconds
}
```

tom_baker: will roll to canary in 5.
priya_shah: also we should backfill the cache key mapping for the last 24h of traffic for key reconciliation — i.e., map old normalized keys -> new normalized keys so old entries remain usable.
maya_li: mapping seems tricky if the difference is whitespace; but we can canonicalize both sides and link them. create a reconciliation job that scans recent keys and writes alias entries.
alex_nguyen: done a quick script on staging that created alias keys for 6k prefixes, hit-rate recovered to 85% for those prefixes.

maya_li: ok next — longer-term: add unit tests around token-normalizer + kernel selection, and a small integration test that asserts cache-key invariants across tokenizers.
priya_shah: +1. also add a perf regression alert if hit-rate delta > 10% for 10m window.

alex_nguyen: monitoring plan — added dashboard: PrefixCache:hit_rate by region, and alert: "prefix_cache_region_drop" firing when region_delta > 0.1 for 10m.
infra-bot: alert created: prefix_cache_region_drop (eu-west)

tom_baker: can we avoid future reliance on exact prompt string in key? maybe hash normalized token ids instead of raw string to be robust to whitespace and unicode NFKC differences.
maya_li: hashing token ids is better but will increase key generation CPU slightly. tradeoff seems worth it.
priya_shah: let's prototype hashing approach in a microservice and compare latency. schedule a perf bench.

alex_nguyen: immediate action items:
- priya: coordinate normalization hotfix + small canary (ETA 1h)
- tom: apply routing override + feature flag (ETA 30m)
- maya: launch primer job for top-5 shards eu-west and reconciliation job (ETA 45m)
- alex: add alerting + staging integration tests (ETA 2h)

maya_li: assigning in tracker: RT-3813 for hotfix, RT-3814 for routing, RT-3815 for primer, RT-3816 for tests/alerting.

priya_shah: started hotfix branch, running unit tests now. quick note — needs to be backward compatible for dedicated customers with pinned runtime.

alex_nguyen: FYI I also noticed kernel-selection changed default batching heuristics which slightly increased prefix cache churn at high concurrency — will open follow-up issue to tune continuous-batching threshold.

maya_li: thanks all. keep updates here. ping me if primer causes unexpected token storm.
alex_nguyen: will post post-mortem summary once metrics stabilize.

infra-bot: deploybot: prefer_warm_affinity canary rolled to 3% traffic @ 03:28 UTC

tom_baker: canary looks good. eu-west hit-rate up 12% in 6m after primer. leaving canary for 20m then ramp.

maya_li: awesome. closing loop later with numbers. :thumbsup:"
